title: Group Self-Service for Jira
body:
For Jira admins and project admins. This is the home of the Group Self-Service for Jira documentation. Learn what the app does, who it is for and where to start.

Group Self-Service for Jira: project admins manage their own groups, with guardrails, an audit log and one-click undo.

Groups and roles, managed where the project lives

In most Jira sites only Jira admins can create groups or change who is in them. So project admins file a ticket for every new teammate. Group Self-Service for Jira lets project admins manage their own project's groups and roles, right in the project settings. You set the rules as a Jira admin. Every change is checked, written to an audit log and can be undone. Depending on your setup, project admins' group changes apply at once or wait until a Jira admin applies them with one click.

How it works

From setup to everyday use in four steps.

🧩 Groups that belong to the project

A project group with its review status and where it is used.

Project admins create groups named atlassian-<PROJECTKEY>-<name>, add and remove people, and set end dates. Before anyone is removed, the app shows where the group grants access: permission schemes, workflows, roles, Confluence and more.

👥 Who is in which group

The People table: plan changes across all groups, then review and apply.

One table shows every person and every project group. Plan additions and removals, give a new colleague the same groups as someone else, or remove a leaver from all groups. Nothing changes until you click Review & apply.

📜 Every change on record

The project's audit log with filters and CSV export.

Each change is logged with who did it, for whom and when. Filter the log and export it as CSV. Auditors get their own read-only page. Most changes can be undone from the message that appears right after them.

 #FFF4EE:busts_in_silhouette:

For project admins

  • Create your project's groups and decide who is in them.
  • Add people for a limited time; they are removed when the end date passes.
  • Add and remove people and groups in your project's roles.
  • Answer access requests and run access reviews.

Start with the User guide.

 #EAF2FF:gear:

For Jira admins

  • Decide how project admins' group changes apply: at once with your account, or after you review them.
  • Choose the projects, protect important groups and mark groups your identity provider manages.
  • See the audit log and a compliance overview for all projects.
  • Move all app data to another installation with an encrypted export.

Start with Getting started.

Explore the documentation

title: Group Self-Service – Getting started
body:
For Jira admins. You will install Group Self-Service for Jira, understand what Jira asks you to approve, and finish the 3-step setup so your project admins can start.

 2

Before you start

  • You need a Jira Cloud site and the Administer Jira permission (you are a Jira admin).
  • Plan about 5 minutes.
  • Optional: if your site also has Confluence, you can install the app there too. The app then also shows where a group is used in Confluence (space permissions and restricted pages).

Step 1: Install the app

Group Self-Service for Jira is available on the Atlassian Marketplace.

  1. In Jira, open Settings (⚙️) → Apps.
  2. Search the Marketplace for Group Self-Service for Jira.
  3. Click the app, then start the free trial or buy it.
  4. Review the permissions Jira shows you (see below) and confirm.

Without an active licence the app stays visible, but nobody can make changes and the scheduled jobs (end dates, clean-up) do not run. You manage the licence under Jira settings → Apps → Manage apps.

What Jira asks you to approve, and why

During installation Jira lists the permissions the app needs. In plain words:

Jira showsWhat the app does with it
Read user informationFind people by name or email when you add them, and show whether an account is active or deactivated.
Read Jira project and work dataRead your projects and the shared filters and dashboards that use a group.
Manage Jira configuration, including acting on behalf of a userRead permission schemes, notification schemes and project roles to show where a group is used. Make group and role changes with the rights of the person who makes them. "On behalf of a user" is only used for the optional automatic changes: a Jira admin lets project admins' changes run with that admin's account. More in the Admin guide.
Delete project role membersLet project admins remove people and groups from their own project's roles on the Roles tab.
Read workflows and issue securityShow which workflows and security levels use a group.
Store app dataKeep the app's settings and audit log in Atlassian's storage for Forge apps.
Read Confluence spaces and pagesOnly when the app is installed in Confluence: show which spaces and restricted pages use a group.

The app never asks for a password or any other credential. It talks to no servers outside Atlassian. Details are on Security & privacy.

Step 2: Finish the 3-step setup

Open Jira settings (⚙️) → Apps → Group Self-Service for Jira. On a new site the page starts with the checklist Get started in 3 steps.

  1. Allow the app to act as you. Click Grant access and confirm Jira's Allow access prompt. Jira asks every Jira admin once, before the app may change groups with their rights.
  2. Choose how project admins' changes apply. Pick one:
    • Apply at once with my account GreenRecommended Project admins' group changes, ended memberships and the clean-up of deactivated accounts run at once, with your account. The app stores no password, only which account to use. You can stop it at any time.
    • I'll review each change: project admins' group changes wait under Changes to apply until a Jira admin applies or rejects them.
  3. Tell your project admins. Click Copy message and paste the short note into chat or email. It tells them where to find the app. If your browser blocks copying, the text appears so you can select and copy it yourself.

Click Done. Everything else already has safe defaults. To see the checklist again, click Setup checklist at the top of the admin page.

Why is this choice needed? Atlassian only lets Jira admins create groups and change their members. Your own changes as a Jira admin always apply at once. Project roles are different: project admins change their own project's roles at once, with their own rights.

Step 3 (optional): Check the defaults

Scroll down on the Configuration tab. The settings you may want to look at first:

SettingDefaultChange it if…
Enabled projectsAll projectsyou want to try the app in a few projects first (Selected projects only).
Blocked groupsAtlassian admin and product access groups are always blockedother groups must never be touched by the app (Additionally blocked).
Synchronised groupsEmptyyour identity provider (for example Entra ID or Okta) manages some groups. They then show as read-only.
AI features (Rovo agent)Offyou want project admins to manage groups in a chat with Rovo.

Click Save after any change. The Admin guide explains every setting.

Step 4 (optional): Install in Confluence

To see Confluence space permissions and restricted pages under Used in, install the app in Confluence on the same site as well. Until then those two checks show App not installed in Confluence. After installation the app builds its page index in the background, in hourly steps.

Where to find the app in Jira

WhoWhereWhat
Project adminsProject → Project settings → Apps → Group Self-Service for JiraGroups, People, Roles, Requests and the project's audit log
Project membersProject → tab My groups (next to Summary, Board, List)Their own groups and access requests
Jira adminsJira settings (⚙️) → Apps → Group Self-Service for JiraConfiguration, Changes to apply, audit log of all projects
AuditorsJira sidebar → Apps → Group audit logRead-only audit log of all projects
Rovo users (if turned on)Rovo → agent Group Self-Service for JiraGroup management in a chat

What project admins see: their project's groups on the left, the selected group with its review status and where it is used on the right.

You're done when…

#E9F7EF:white_check_mark:
  • The checklist on the admin page says All set.
  • A project admin opens Project settings → Apps → Group Self-Service for Jira and sees the Groups tab.
  • A test change shows up in Audit log (all projects) on the admin page. If you chose to review changes, it first appears under Changes to apply.

The first time someone opens a page of the app, a short guided tour shows them around. They can start it again with Tutorial.

💬 Need help? Open a request in the SUPERPORT support portal.

Documentation by George Papasotiriou, developer of Group Self-Service for Jira · SUPERPORT

title: Group Self-Service – User guide
body:
For project admins, with short parts for project members and auditors. You will learn how to create groups, add and remove people, manage your project's roles, answer access requests and find every change in the audit log.

 2

Open the app

Go to your project → Project settings → Apps → Group Self-Service for Jira. You need the Administer Projects permission in the project.

The page has these tabs:

TabWhat you do there
GroupsCreate groups, add and remove people, see where a group is used.
PeopleSee who is in which group and change many memberships at once.
RolesAdd and remove people and groups in your project's roles (if your Jira admin left this on).
RequestsApprove or deny access requests from project members.
Waiting for Jira adminOnly shown when your group changes wait for a Jira admin. See When your changes wait for a Jira admin below.
Audit logEvery change in your project.

At the top you also find Member view (shows the page as project members see it), Tutorial (restarts the guided tour) and, if your Jira admin turned on AI features, Ask Rovo.

Will my change apply at once?

Atlassian only lets Jira admins create groups and change their members. Your Jira admin chose one of two ways for your site:

What you changeAutomatic changes onReview by a Jira admin
Groups and their membersGreenAt onceYellowWaits until a Jira admin applies it
Project rolesGreenAt onceGreenAt once

When your changes wait, the page shows the note Changes you make here wait for a Jira administrator at the top. Either way, the same rules apply and every change is in the audit log.

Create a group

  1. Click Create group (top right).
  2. Type the last part of the name. The prefix atlassian-<PROJECTKEY>- is added for you.
    • Up to 30 lowercase letters, digits and hyphens.
    • Start and end with a letter or digit, no double hyphens.
    • Wait for the green Name is available.
  3. Optional: add a Description (what the group is for).
  4. Optional: under Start with the members of, pick another group of your project to copy its members (up to 50 people; end dates are not copied).
  5. Leave Add me as the first member ticked if you want to be in the group.
  6. Click Create group. If your changes wait for a Jira admin, the button says Request group and the group appears under Requested groups until it is created.

The name cannot be changed later, and only Jira admins can delete a group (in Atlassian Administration). The group is a normal Atlassian group, available in Jira, Confluence and Jira Service Management.

A new group may show Being set up at Atlassian for a minute or two. That is normal.

Check where a group is used

Click a group on the left. Under Used in the app checks 9 places: permission schemes, workflows, project roles, security levels, notification schemes, shared filters, shared dashboards, Confluence spaces and restricted Confluence pages. Click a card for details, or Refresh to check again.

A group with its description, a due access review and the places it is used in.

Could not be checked or No permission to check is not the same as "not used". Check again with Refresh, or ask your Jira admin.

Add people to a group

  1. On the Groups tab, click the group.
  2. In Add people, type at least 2 letters of a name or email and pick the person. Pick several to add them together.
  3. Optional: set Access to 7, 30 or 90 days, or Until date…. The person is removed after that date. Leave No end date for permanent access.
  4. Click Add.

Adding many people? Click Paste a list, paste up to 50 emails or names (one per line or separated by commas) and click Check. Choose the right person for rows marked Several matches, please choose, then click Add N people.

Does the group show Also grants access in other projects? Then only a Jira admin can add people to it, so access cannot spread beyond your project. Removing people still works.

Remove people from a group

One person: click the remove button (✕) next to the person. The app shows what they lose, for example a permission scheme or a project role. Click Remove.

Before removing someone, the app shows which schemes and roles the group grants rights in.

Several people (access review):

  1. Click Review access.
  2. Tick the people who no longer need access, then click Review removal….
  3. Check What they lose and add a Note for the audit log, for example "Q4 access review".
  4. Tick I checked that these people no longer need this access.
  5. Click Remove N people.

Change or remove an end date

Click the calendar icon next to a member, pick a new date or No end date, then click Save.

After the end date, the person is removed in the next hourly run. If your group changes wait for a Jira admin, the person is marked Access ended – removal waiting for a Jira admin until a Jira admin applies the removal.

Change many memberships at once (People tab)

The People tab shows Who is in which group: one row per person, one column per group.

  1. Click cells to plan changes. An empty cell becomes will be added, a filled cell will be removed.
    • To remove someone from everything, use the ✕ at the end of their row (Plan to remove … from all groups).
    • To add someone who is not in the table yet, use Add a person to the table….
    • Tick several people to get Add to group, Remove from group, Same groups as… (a new colleague gets the groups of a team member; nothing is taken away) and Remove from all groups.
    • Many groups? Groups N/M chooses which groups are columns. Bulk actions still reach every group.
    • Planned something by mistake? Undo step (or Ctrl+Z) takes back the last step.
  2. Nothing has changed yet. Click Review & apply.
  3. Optional: set an end date for the additions and add a note. For removals, tick the confirmation.
  4. Click Apply N changes. Up to 100 changes fit in one batch.

The People table with one planned removal, ready for Review & apply.

Changes that fail stay planned so you can try again. Undo batch reverses the whole batch. Use the filters Deactivated, Ending in 14 days and Changed to focus.

Manage your project's roles (Roles tab)

The Roles tab lists your project's roles, for example Administrators or Developers, with the people and groups in each. Roles control access inside this project through its permission scheme. Changes here apply at once with your own Jira rights, just like in Jira's project settings.

  • Add people: pick a role, type at least 2 letters of a name or email, choose one or more people and click Add.
  • Remove a person: click the remove button next to them and confirm. You cannot remove yourself; ask another project admin.
  • Add a group: under Add a group, type a group name. Your project's own groups come first, marked This project's group. Click Add group. Everyone in the group gets the role.
  • Remove a group: click the remove button next to it and confirm.
  • To change who is in one of your project's groups, click Open group.

Groups marked Protected (admin and product access groups, and groups your Jira admin blocked) can only be changed by a Jira admin, in Jira's project settings. The first time, Jira may ask you to allow the app to act as you: click Grant access and confirm Allow access.

Answer access requests

When project members ask to join a group, the Requests tab shows a number.

  1. Open Requests and read the reason and the requested duration.
  2. Click Approve to add the person with the requested end date, or Deny and give a Reason for the person.

You can undo every decision under Decided in the last 90 days. If your changes wait for a Jira admin, an approved request shows Approved – waiting for a Jira admin, and the end date starts when the Jira admin applies it.

Complete a periodic access review

If your Jira admin turned on periodic reviews, groups that are due show Review due.

  1. Open the group and click Review now.
  2. Remove anyone who no longer needs access (see Remove people from a group). Tick Also record this as the group's periodic access review to count it.
  3. Otherwise confirm that everyone left still needs access and click Record review.

Edit a group's description

Open the group and click Edit description (or Add a description). Press Ctrl + Enter to save or Esc to cancel.

When your changes wait for a Jira admin

If your Jira admin reviews project admins' changes, your group changes are not in Jira until a Jira admin applies them.

  • Copy link for your Jira admin at the top copies a link to the page where they apply changes. Send it by chat or email.
  • A group with waiting changes shows a box Waiting for a Jira administrator, listing who will be added or will be removed.
  • You can Withdraw your own changes while they wait: in the message right after the change, in the waiting box or on the Waiting for Jira admin tab.
  • Applied and rejected changes appear under Recently decided, with the Jira admin's note if they rejected it.

Every rule is checked when you ask and again when the Jira admin applies it.

Undo a change

After most changes a message appears with Undo. Click it to reverse the change; people also get back their previous end date. Waiting changes show Withdraw instead. Missed the message? The audit log shows exactly what changed, so you can add or remove the person again.

See the history

The Audit log tab lists every change in your project. Filter by Period, Group, Action or Person and click Export CSV. Entries cannot be changed. To download a group's member list, use the download button next to Review access (Export members as CSV).

The project audit log: time, action, group, affected person and who made the change.

For project members: My groups

Open your project and click the tab My groups (next to Summary, Board and List). You see the project's groups you are in, and when your access ends.

  1. Under Request access, find the group you need and click Request.
  2. Fill in Why do you need access? and choose For how long?: 7, 30 or 90 days, or no end date.
  3. Click Send request. A project admin decides; you see the result under Your requests. Changed your mind? Click Withdraw.

My groups: a member's own groups and the groups they can request access to.

No My groups page or Request button? Your Jira admin switched these off. Ask a project admin directly.

For auditors: the Group audit log

Open the Jira sidebar → Apps → Group audit log. You get a read-only log of all projects. Filter by Period, Project, Group, Action or Person and click Export CSV. If you see No access, ask your Jira admin to add you to an auditor group.

Ask Rovo (optional)

If your Jira admin turned on AI features, click Ask Rovo or open Rovo and choose the agent Group Self-Service for Jira. Ask in English or German, for example "Where is atlassian-ABC-reviewers used?" or "Add anna@example.com to atlassian-ABC-reviewers for 30 days."

  • The agent always says what it will do and waits for your OK before changing anything.
  • It never guesses between people with similar names.
  • It has the same rights and limits as you in the app. Its changes are marked via Rovo in the audit log.

AI answers can be wrong. Check what the agent plans before you confirm.

Good to know

  • Groups marked IdP sync are managed by your identity provider. You can see their members but not change them.
  • Atlassian admin and product access groups, and groups your Jira admin blocked, are never shown or changed by the app.
  • The app shows groups whose names start with atlassian-<PROJECTKEY>-. If your project key changed, groups created under the old key stay with your project and show created under key ….

💬 Need help? Open a request in the SUPERPORT support portal.

Documentation by George Papasotiriou, developer of Group Self-Service for Jira · SUPERPORT

title: Group Self-Service – Admin guide
body:
For Jira admins. You will learn every setting of Group Self-Service for Jira, how project admins' changes reach Jira, how to work the change queue, and how to use the audit log, the licence and the data export.

 2

Open the admin page

Go to Jira settings (⚙️) → Apps → Group Self-Service for Jira. The page has three tabs: Configuration, Changes to apply and Audit log (all projects). When changes wait for a Jira admin, the page opens on Changes to apply.

On a new site, the Get started in 3 steps checklist is shown first (see Getting started). Bring it back any time with Setup checklist at the top.

Who can do what

PersonHow the app recognises themWhat they can do
Jira adminAdminister Jira global permissionEverything: configuration, change queue, all audit logs, export and import. Their own group changes apply at once with their own rights, in every project.
Project adminAdminister Projects in the projectManage the groups and roles of their own project only, within your rules.
Project memberCan browse the projectSee their own groups on My groups and request access (if turned on).
AuditorMember of an Auditor groupRead and export the audit log of all projects, nothing else.

Decide how group changes are made

Atlassian only lets Jira admins create groups and change their members. So in the section How group changes are made you decide what happens with project admins' group changes:

ModeWhat happens
Jira administrators apply changesProject admins' changes (new groups, additions, removals, approved access requests) and the automatic removals wait under Changes to apply. A Jira admin applies or rejects them.
Apply project admins' changes automaticallyThe same changes run at once, with the account of the Jira admin who switched this on, as if they applied them by hand.

In both modes: your own changes as a Jira admin always apply at once, and project role changes always run with the project admin's own rights.

Switch on automatic changes

  1. Under Apply project admins' changes automatically, click Use my account. (Another admin's account is in use? Click Use my account instead.)
  2. The app first checks that Jira lets it act for your account. The section then shows On, with your account (since …).
#EAF2FF:shield:

Safeguards

  • The app stores no password or other credential, only which account to use.
  • Only a Jira admin can switch it on, and only for their own account. Any Jira admin can click Stop.
  • Project admins keep all their limits: only their own project's groups, the scope check, blocked and IdP groups.
  • Before each change the app checks that the account is still an active Jira admin. Jira checks that admin's rights on every call.
  • Every change is in the audit log with the project admin who made it and (applied as …) the account used.

Paused? Automatic changes pause by themselves when the account can no longer apply changes. Changes then wait under Changes to apply again. The section shows why:

Shown reasonWhat to do
… is no longer a Jira admin.A current Jira admin clicks Use my account.
the account of … is deactivated.A current Jira admin clicks Use my account.
… withdrew the app's access to their account.That admin (or another) clicks Use my account and allows access when Jira asks.

Changes that were already waiting when you switch on automatic changes stay under Changes to apply.

Allow the app to act as you

Group changes run with your own Jira rights. Jira asks every Jira admin once to allow this. When the page shows Allow the app to act as you, click Grant access and confirm Allow access in Jira's prompt. If Jira shows no prompt, reload the page and allow access when Jira asks.

Apply or reject waiting changes

The tab Changes to apply (also shown as N waiting at the top) lists everything that waits for a Jira admin, from all projects. Each entry shows the group and project, who asked and when, and the reason. Automatic marks the hourly end-date job and the deactivated-account clean-up; via Rovo marks the Rovo agent.

  • Apply runs the change with your rights and checks every rule again. If the result is already in place, the change is marked as applied without an error.
  • Reject asks for an optional Note for the project admin. Rejecting an Access ended removal keeps the person and removes their end date. Rejecting an Account deactivated removal keeps that account; the clean-up does not ask again.
  • Tick several entries, or Select all, to apply or reject up to 100 at once. Each change gets its own result. Anything that fails stays in the list with the reason.

On each project page, Jira admins also see N changes by project admins wait for a Jira admin (all projects) with a button that opens the list. Decided changes stay visible under Recently decided for 90 days.

Choose the projects

Under Enabled projects, choose All projects (default) or Selected projects only and pick the projects. In other projects, project admins see The app is not enabled for this project.

Naming convention

Groups are always named atlassian-<PROJECTKEY>-<name>. Project admins only choose the last part (up to 30 characters). This is fixed. Renaming and deleting are not possible in the app; delete groups in Atlassian Administration when needed.

Protect groups

Blocked groups

The app can neither show nor change blocked groups.

  • Always blocked: Atlassian core groups for administration (for example site-admins, jira-administrators) and the product access groups (for example jira-software-users, confluence-users). You cannot remove them from the list.
  • Additionally blocked: your own additions. Click Block a group and enter a group name or a pattern with a * at the start or end, like jira-admins-*.

Synchronised groups (IdP/SCIM)

Under Synchronised groups, add the groups (or patterns) your identity provider manages, for example from Entra ID or Okta. The app shows them as IdP sync: members are visible, but nobody can change them in the app.

Roles & features

SettingDefaultWhat it does
Show the "My groups" page to project membersOnMembers see their own groups (read-only) in the project tab My groups.
Project admins manage their project's roles ("Roles" tab)OnProject admins add and remove people and groups in their project's roles, at once and with their own Jira rights. Protected groups stay off-limits.
Allow time-limited membershipsOnProject admins can set end dates. Ended memberships are removed by the hourly job (at once with automatic changes, otherwise as a waiting removal).
Project admins can only add people to groups that grant access within their own project (scope check)On (recommended)A project group that also appears in another project's permission scheme or roles is locked for additions by project admins. Jira admins can still change it; removing people always works.
Auditor groupsNoneMembers of these groups can read and export the audit log of all projects. They find it under Apps → Group audit log. Open the audit log page takes you there.

AI features (Rovo agent)

The Rovo agent Group Self-Service for Jira lets project admins manage groups in a chat. It is GreyOff by default.

  1. In the section AI features (Rovo agent), tick Turn on AI features.
  2. Click Save.

While it is off, the Ask Rovo button is hidden and the agent refuses every request. When on, the agent uses the same permission checks as the app, confirms before every change, and adds at most 10 or removes at most 5 people per request. AI results can be wrong and must be reviewed.

Governance & automation

SettingDefaultWhat it does
Project members can request access to project groupsOnMembers can ask to join a group from My groups, with a reason and 7, 30 or 90 days or no end date. Project admins decide.
Periodic access reviewOffEvery 3, 6 or 12 months, project admins confirm who still needs each group. Due groups show Review due.
Remove deactivated accounts from app groups automatically (daily)OffRemoves deactivated accounts from the groups this app manages, never from blocked or IdP groups. Click Who would be removed? for a dry run first, then Switch on. Without automatic changes, each removal waits under Changes to apply (reason Account deactivated).

Settings take effect after you click Save.

Compliance overview

The Compliance overview shows, across all projects: access reviews due, memberships that end within 14 days, open access requests, and the status of the Confluence page index. Click a card for details. Rebuild rebuilds the Confluence index in the background, in hourly steps.

Audit log and retention

Every change is written to the audit log: groups created, people added and removed, end dates, requests, reviews, role changes, waiting changes, configuration changes, exports and imports. Entries cannot be edited. The tab Audit log (all projects) lets you filter by Period, Project, Group, Action or Person and Export CSV.

The audit log, here in a project. Entries marked "via Rovo" came from the Rovo agent.

Under Audit log retention choose Never delete (default) or Delete after a number of months. Older entries are removed automatically every day. This is the only way entries are ever deleted.

Save and undo configuration changes

Nothing takes effect until you click Save. Discard drops unsaved changes. Each save is logged in the audit log, and you can undo it from the message that appears.

Scheduled jobs

JobHow often
Remove memberships whose end date has passedHourly
Build the Confluence page restriction index (only if installed in Confluence)Hourly
Remove deactivated accounts (if switched on)Daily
Delete audit entries older than the retention period (if set)Daily

Licence

Group Self-Service for Jira is a paid app. Without an active licence, every page shows This site has no active licence for Group Self-Service for Jira, so changes are switched off. You can still view everything. The scheduled jobs do not run either. To turn changes back on, start a free trial or subscribe under Jira settings → Apps → Manage apps.

Maintenance and service status

If SUPERPORT ever has to pause the app to keep your data safe, users see a maintenance page or a notice that changes are paused, with a link to the status page. Nothing you saved is lost. Follow updates on superapps.statuspage.io.

Move data to another installation (export & import)

Use Export & import data on the Configuration tab to move everything the app has stored to another installation on the same site: settings, group assignments, descriptions, end dates, requests, reviews, waiting changes and the complete audit log. Only Jira admins see this section.

Export

  1. Click Export all data.
  2. Enter a Passphrase of at least 12 characters and type it again under Repeat passphrase.
  3. Click Encrypt & export and save the file.

Import

  1. In the other installation, click Import from file… and pick the file.
  2. Enter the passphrase and click Decrypt.
  3. Check the summary: number of records and audit entries, who exported it and when.
  4. Tick I want to import this data into this installation. and click Import.

The file is encrypted in your browser (AES-256-GCM) and the passphrase never leaves your browser. Keep the passphrase in your password manager, separate from the file. Without it nobody can open the file, not even SUPERPORT.
  • Only encrypted exports can be imported, and only on the same Atlassian site.
  • Records that already exist in this installation are replaced by the ones in the file. Audit entries that already exist are skipped, so importing twice is safe. If an import stops partway, run it again.
  • Two things are not exported on purpose: the account used for automatic changes and the setup checklist. Set them up again in the new installation.
  • Both export and import are recorded in the audit log.

💬 Need help? Open a request in the SUPERPORT support portal.

title: Group Self-Service – FAQ & troubleshooting
body:
For everyone who uses Group Self-Service for Jira. Find the message you see on screen and learn what it means and what to do. Click a question to open the answer.

 2

Access and setup

I see "Only project admins can manage the groups of this project."

You need the Administer Projects permission in this project. Ask a project admin or your Jira admin. Project members find their own groups in the project tab My groups instead.

 I see "The app is not enabled for this project. Contact your Jira admin."

Your Jira admin limited the app to selected projects. They can add your project under Enabled projects on the app's admin page.

 I see "Allow the app to act on your behalf first: click “Grant access”. Nothing was changed."

Some changes run with your own Jira rights: group changes by Jira admins and role changes by project admins. Jira asks each person once to allow this.

  1. Click Grant access in the notice at the top of the page.
  2. Confirm Allow access in Jira's prompt.
  3. Try your change again.

If Jira shows no prompt, reload the page and allow access when Jira asks.

 I see "This site has no active licence for Group Self-Service for Jira, so changes are switched off."

You can still view everything, but nobody can make changes until the licence is active. A Jira admin starts a free trial or subscribes under Jira settings → Apps → Manage apps.

 I see "Group Self-Service for Jira is temporarily unavailable" or "Changes are paused for maintenance".

SUPERPORT paused the app for maintenance to keep your data safe. Nothing you saved is lost. Follow the progress on the status page; the app is back as soon as possible.

Groups and members

I can't find a group I know exists.

The app only shows groups that belong to your project, named atlassian-<PROJECTKEY>-…. Groups that your Jira admin blocked, and Atlassian admin and product access groups, are never shown.

 A group shows "IdP sync" and I can't change it.

Your identity provider (for example Entra ID or Okta) manages this group. Change its members there. In the app you can only see them.

 My new group shows "Being set up at Atlassian" or "Jira does not know this group (yet)."

Atlassian needs a minute or two before a new group is visible everywhere in Jira. Wait a moment and refresh the page.

 I see "This group also grants access in other projects. Only a Jira admin can add people to it."

Groups are shared across the whole site. This group also appears in another project's permission scheme or roles, so adding people would give them access outside your project. That is why only a Jira admin can add people to it. You can still remove people. Ask your Jira admin, or create a new group just for your project.

 "Used in" says "Could not be checked", "No permission to check" or "App not installed in Confluence".
  • Could not be checked: the check failed this time. Click Refresh.
  • No permission to check: the app is not allowed to read this information on your site.
  • App not installed in Confluence: a Jira admin installs the app in Confluence on the same site to see space permissions and restricted pages.

In all three cases the group may still be used there. Do not read it as "not used".

 When exactly is someone removed after their end date?

The app checks every hour. With automatic changes on, the person is removed in the next hourly run. Otherwise the removal waits for a Jira admin, and the person shows Access ended – removal waiting for a Jira admin until it is applied.

Waiting changes and automatic changes

My change says "Waiting for a Jira admin". Did it work?

Not yet. On your site, a Jira admin applies project admins' group changes. Nothing changes in Jira until they do. Click Copy link for your Jira admin and send them the link. You can withdraw your change while it waits. Role changes are not affected: they always apply at once.

 I see "Automatic changes are paused because the Jira admin’s account can no longer apply changes."

The Jira admin whose account applied your changes is no longer a Jira admin, was deactivated, or withdrew the app's access. Nothing was changed. Try again: your change then waits for a Jira admin. A Jira admin can switch automatic changes on again with Use my account on the admin page.

 When I click "Use my account" I see "Jira did not let the app act with your account outside your session."

Jira did not allow the app to act for your account, so nothing was switched on. First make sure you allowed access (Grant access). If the message stays, contact SUPERPORT support. Until then you can review project admins' changes under Changes to apply.

Project roles

I see "You cannot remove yourself from a role here; ask another project admin."

This protects you from removing your own project admin rights by accident. Another project admin or a Jira admin can remove you.

 A group in a role shows "Protected", or I see "Jira did not allow this role change for you."

Protected groups (admin and product access groups, and groups your Jira admin blocked) can only be changed by a Jira admin, in Jira's project settings. "Jira did not allow this role change" means Jira refused the change for your account: you need the Administer Projects permission in this project.

 The Roles tab is missing or says "Project roles are turned off for this app by your Jira admin."

Your Jira admin switched off Project admins manage their project's roles. You can still manage roles in Jira's own project settings (People).

Audit log, data and AI

I see "Only members of the auditor groups and Jira admins can read the audit log here."

Ask your Jira admin to add you to one of the Auditor groups in the app's configuration. Project admins see their own project's log on the Audit log tab in the project settings.

 An import fails with "Wrong passphrase", "different Atlassian site" or "not encrypted".
  • Wrong passphrase, or the file was changed after export. Check the passphrase. If it is right, the file was damaged or changed: export again.
  • This export comes from a different Atlassian site. Exports only work on the same site, because group and account IDs belong to their site.
  • This export is not encrypted. Only encrypted exports can be imported. Export again from the original installation.

If an import stops partway, just start it again. Entries that are already there are skipped.

 There is no "Ask Rovo" button, or Rovo says the AI features are turned off.

AI features are off by default. A Jira admin turns them on under AI features (Rovo agent) on the app's admin page and clicks Save. If the admin page says Temporarily turned off by the app vendor, your setting is kept and applies again once AI is available.

💬 Need help? Open a request in the SUPERPORT support portal.

Documentation by George Papasotiriou, developer of Group Self-Service for Jira · SUPERPORT

title: Group Self-Service – Security & privacy
body:
For Jira admins, security and privacy teams. You will learn where Group Self-Service for Jira runs, what it stores, which permissions it uses and why, and how it protects your groups.

 2

Where the app runs and where data is stored

#E9F7EF:lock:
  • The app is built on Atlassian Forge and runs on Atlassian's cloud.
  • It talks to no servers outside Atlassian: it only calls Jira (and Confluence, if installed there).
  • Its data is kept in Atlassian's storage for Forge apps: settings and records in Forge storage, the audit log in a Forge SQL database.
  • The app never asks for, stores or uses a password or any other credential.

What the app stores

DataContentsKept until
ConfigurationYour settings: enabled projects, blocked and synchronised groups, auditor groups, features, retention.Changed or uninstalled
Project groupsGroup ID and name, the project it belongs to, who created it and when, description, last access review.Group no longer exists
End datesGroup, account ID, end date and who set it.The membership ends or the date is removed
Access requestsRequester, group, reason, requested duration, decision and notes.Not deleted automatically
Waiting changesWhat a project admin asked for, who and when, notes, the decision.90 days after the decision
Audit logTime, action, project, group, the affected person's account ID and name, who made the change, and details such as notes or applied as.Your retention setting (default: never deleted)
Automatic changesAccount ID and name of the Jira admin whose account is used. No credentials.A Jira admin stops it
Usage resultsWhere a group is used, kept briefly so pages load fast; for Confluence, an index of restricted pages (page ID, title, space).Refreshed automatically
Small user preferencesWhether a person has seen the guided tour; the state of the admin setup checklist.Uninstall

Personal data

  • The app works with Atlassian account IDs and display names. It shows names and email addresses as Jira provides them, according to each person's Atlassian profile visibility.
  • The audit log keeps account IDs and display names of the people who make changes and of the people affected. Access requests keep the reason a person typed.
  • CSV exports (audit log, group members) are downloaded to the computer of the person who exports them. A member export contains names, account IDs, email addresses (where visible), status and end dates.
  • A Jira admin decides how long audit entries are kept (Audit log retention).

Permissions (scopes) and why the app needs them

PermissionWhy
read:jira-userFind people when adding them; show active or deactivated accounts.
read:jira-workRead projects, shared filters and dashboards for the usage check.
manage:jira-configuration (with acting on behalf of a user)Read schemes and roles for the usage check; create groups and change members and roles with the rights of the user who makes the change. Acting on behalf of a user is used only for the optional automatic changes.
delete:project-role:jiraRemove people and groups from project roles on the Roles tab.
read:workflow:jira, read:issue-security-scheme:jira, read:issue-security-level:jiraShow which workflows and security levels use a group.
storage:appStore the app's data in Forge storage.
Confluence read permissions (spaces, space permissions, pages)Only when installed in Confluence: show which spaces and restricted pages use a group.

How changes are made

  • Jira admins change groups with their own rights. Jira asks each of them once to allow the app to act as them.
  • Project admins' group changes either wait until a Jira admin applies them, or, with automatic changes on, run with the account of the Jira admin who switched this on.
  • Project role changes always run with the project admin's own rights, exactly as in Jira's project settings.

Safeguards for automatic changes

  • Only a Jira admin can switch it on, and only for their own account. Any Jira admin can stop it.
  • Before each use, the app checks that the account is still an active Jira admin. Jira checks that admin's rights on every call. If either check fails, automatic changes pause by themselves and changes wait again.
  • Every change is logged with the project admin who made it and the account it was applied as.

Guardrails inside the app

  • Project, account and site come from Atlassian, never from the browser.
  • Every change checks again that the person is a project admin of that project and that the group belongs to the project.
  • Atlassian admin and product access groups are always blocked. Blocked and identity-provider groups are never changed: not in the app, not by the Rovo agent, not by the scheduled jobs.
  • The scope check stops project admins from adding people to groups that also grant access in other projects.
  • All rules are checked when a change is requested and again when it is applied.
  • The audit log is append-only. Its only deletion is the retention period you set.

AI (Rovo agent)

  • The Rovo agent is off by default. A Jira admin decides whether to turn it on.
  • It runs in Atlassian Rovo and acts as the person using it, with the same permission checks as the app.
  • It confirms before every change, never guesses between similar names, and adds at most 10 or removes at most 5 people per request.
  • Its changes are marked via Rovo in the audit log. AI answers can be wrong and must be reviewed.

Data export

  • Only Jira admins can export or import, checked on every step, and both are recorded in the audit log.
  • Exports are always encrypted in the browser with AES-256-GCM. The key comes from a passphrase of at least 12 characters (PBKDF2-SHA-256, 600,000 iterations).
  • The passphrase never leaves the browser. Changed files fail to open. Unencrypted files and files from another site are refused.

Uninstalling

  • Groups the app created are normal Atlassian groups. They and their members stay after you uninstall the app.
  • The app's settings and audit log are no longer available in Jira after you uninstall. To keep them, use Export all data first (see the Admin guide).

Legal

  • End User License Agreement (covers all SUPERPORT apps)
  • Vendor: SUPERPORT P.C., Athens, Greece · www.superport.digital

💬 Need help? Open a request in the SUPERPORT support portal or email support@superport.digital.

title: Group Self-Service – Release notes
body:
For Jira admins and project admins. What changed in Group Self-Service for Jira, newest first.

4.1.0 · 23 November 2026

  • GreenNEW Automatic changes. A Jira admin can let project admins' group changes, ended memberships and the deactivated-account clean-up apply at once, with their own account. No password is stored, the app checks the account before each change, pauses by itself if needed, and any Jira admin can stop it.
  • GreenNEW Roles tab. Project admins add and remove people and groups in their own project's roles, at once and with their own Jira rights. Protected groups stay locked. Every change is in the audit log and can be undone.
  • GreenNEW Get started in 3 steps. New sites open the admin page on a short checklist: allow access, choose how project admins' changes apply, and copy a ready-made message for your project admins.
  • BlueIMPROVED Waiting changes: project admins can Copy link for your Jira admin; Jira admins see how many changes wait on every project page; the admin page opens on Changes to apply when something waits.
  • BlueIMPROVED Updated guided tours for project admins and Jira admins.

Upgrading from a 3.x version: Jira asks a Jira admin to approve updated permissions (removing people and groups from project roles, and acting on behalf of a user for automatic changes). Until then, Jira keeps the previous version.

3.18 · 20 November 2026

  • GreenNEW Jira admins apply changes. Group changes now run through Jira with each Jira admin's own rights. Project admins' changes, approved access requests and automatic removals wait under Changes to apply, where a Jira admin applies or rejects them, one by one or several at once. Every rule is checked again when applying.
  • GreenNEW Project admins see their waiting changes on the Waiting for Jira admin tab and can withdraw them.
  • BlueIMPROVED An Allow access notice appears wherever a Jira admin's change needs Jira's one-time consent.
  • PurpleFIXED Review & apply on the People tab no longer shows an empty page; planned changes read "planned" again.

3.13.0 · 16 November 2026

  • BlueIMPROVED AI features (Rovo agent) have their own section on the admin page and are off by default, also on existing installations. While off, the Ask Rovo button and the Rovo hints are hidden.

Early November 2026

  • BlueIMPROVED Without an active licence, every page says so up front (with a hint for Jira admins) and scheduled jobs pause.
  • BlueIMPROVED If the app is ever paused for maintenance, users see a clear notice with a link to the status page.

30 October 2026

  • GreenNEW New name: Group Self-Service for Jira, with a new icon.
  • GreenNEW People tab: choose which groups are columns, select people for Add to group, Remove from group, Same groups as… and Remove from all groups, and Undo step (Ctrl+Z).
  • GreenNEW Scope check: project admins cannot add people to groups that also grant access in other projects (configurable; removing always works).
  • GreenNEW Rovo agent: a person's groups, same groups as, offboarding, copy members and undo last change. Bulk actions show a preview first.
  • BlueIMPROVED Group name part limited to 30 characters, with a counter.
  • PurpleFIXED Dropdowns no longer catch the next click, and the page no longer freezes after creating a group from a copy source.

27 October 2026

  • GreenNEW Guided tour for first-time users on every page of the app, available again any time with Tutorial.
  • GreenNEW Export & import data for Jira admins, always encrypted with a passphrase.

26 October 2026 · First release

  • Project groups with a fixed naming convention, member management with end dates, paste-a-list and access reviews.
  • Usage check in 9 places, and the impact shown before anyone is removed.
  • People table, access requests from project members, periodic access reviews, clean-up of deactivated accounts.
  • Append-only audit log with CSV export and a read-only page for auditors; Undo for every change.
  • Rovo agent; English and German; light and dark theme.

💬 Need help? Open a request in the SUPERPORT support portal.

Documentation by George Papasotiriou, developer of Group Self-Service for Jira · SUPERPORT
